source.original_title: 05/07/2026 - Soneel Raj & Farooq Bey KFS- Kettlebell Body Game Plan Session
source.display_title: 05/07/2026 - Soneel Raj & Farooq Bey KFS- Kettlebell Body Game Plan Session — Follow Up

call.sequence_note: First of TWO separate sales calls contained in this single recording file, running 00:00:00 to 00:56:02. A second, unrelated prospect (Engin Oytac) joins at 00:56:14 and is extracted separately as 2026-05-07_engin-oytac_farooq-bey.

setter.name: Kim Forbes-Sobers
setter.evidence: And Kim was very good about chasing me, if I got his name right. And then that's how we got on today. Also: 'he did send me a link, which I completely transparently didn't get a chance to watch... Kim did. He sent it to me via email, via text.' Note the prospect uses 'he' for Kim, and separately 'In fact, I had mentioned that to Kim because I was trying, and he said today's available, so that's why I jumped on it.'

prospect.name: Soneel Raj
prospect.location: Florida, USA (Eastern time). Grew up in India; lived in Singapore for around eight years.
prospect.occupation: Senior transformation executive — runs large technology organisations, typically brought in by an incoming CEO to turn around the P&L over two to three years. Not currently employed: a three-year non-compete from his last role ended in December. Currently acting as subject-matter expert on a private equity acquisition due diligence, and expects to take a senior role within three to six months.
prospect.family_status: Married; wife trains every day and is in good shape. Three children; eldest son visiting and about to start an investment banking job. Mother died in November, in Asia after a period of illness; father lives in India.
prospect.training_background: Lifted weights and worked with a trainer in his 40s, describing himself then as 'one degree less than buff'. Nothing sustained since. Played soccer in college and cricket growing up; plays golf. Bought a Peloton in January and has started riding regularly. Was walking three miles daily with a 25 lb weighted vest and lost seven to eight pounds before knee pain stopped him. Historical weight 150-165 lb. No kettlebell experience.
prospect.medical: Knee pain that stopped his weighted-vest walking. An orthopaedic surgeon friend examined him informally and attributed it to excess weight rather than a knee problem — 'dude, you're fine. You just need to lose weight. It's five X the weight on your knees.' Reports low-grade inflammation 'across the board'. Had a full biomarker panel (Function Health, around 100 markers) in December: broadly clear, but LDL and HDL trending negatively with the added weight, and biological age assessed six years below chronological. Primary care at Mayo Clinic, with a Mayo nutritionist already engaged.

signals: Names the loss in his own words in the first sixty seconds: 'I have kind of let myself go is the best way I can describe it'
Wants a former self back — 150-165 lb historically, 'in my 40s I was in great shape... one degree less than buff'
Trigger is a hard season: his mother died in November and 'I've got three kids and I want to be around for them'
Carries the regret explicitly: 'I should have been doing this physical thing a while ago' and 'if I'm not doing it, it's a choice at this point'
Diverges from the classic rebuilder in method — he is running the decision as a structured consultant's evaluation, sequencing data collection, options and criteria rather than acting on emotion

goals.text: Lose the roughly 20-25 lb gained over recent years and get rid of the belly and chest fat
Rebuild muscle he is losing, having realised walking and cycling alone are not enough
Be around and walking for his three children — his mother reached 89 and he wants to reach that on his feet, not in a wheelchair
Learn kettlebell technique properly without getting hurt
Train anywhere — at home and in hotels while travelling globally for work
Make this a permanent lifestyle change rather than a cycle of getting in shape and losing it again
Feel at peace with himself when he looks in the mirror, shaves or puts on clothes
Get his health sorted in the three-to-six-month window before he starts the next intense transformation role
Strengthen his knees by reducing load on them
Improve his golf, which the belly has made harder

pains.text: Gained roughly 20-25 lb over several years through travel, poor meal timing and not training
Knee pain that forced him to abandon weighted-vest walking, attributed informally to carrying excess weight
Losing muscle mass and unable to reverse it with walking and cycling alone
Not at peace with himself — 'when I look at myself, take a shower, I'm like, I can't, that's not what I like looking at'
Mother died in November after a period of illness; last year described as a blur
Identity vacuum from three years unable to work under a non-compete — 'I am defining myself with what I'm doing' and that piece is missing
Biomarkers trending negatively — LDL and HDL moving the wrong way with the weight
Nearest gym is a thirty-minute drive, and heavy international travel makes any gym routine impractical
Metabolism changed sharply after 55 — 'every time I eat something, it adds a freaking pound the next day if I don't do something'
Self-described laziness when unsupervised — 'if I can sneak away, have that extra carb for the day, I might do it'
Compares unfavourably to his wife, whose biomarker panel put her twelve years below her chronological age against his six

objections.raw_quote: I'm thinking out loud, and I'm sure you've gotten this question, what are you getting from different, from people who can get access to a personal coach for that price? ... if I go to the club, if I price him out three to five times a week, I think I'd be ahead of that 4K number.
objections.rep_response: Used a LeBron James analogy — would you rather learn basketball from a good in-person coach four or five times a week, or from LeBron James online — and argued more touchpoints than an in-person client because you get Trevor's phone number.

objections.raw_quote: Let me do this. I will give it some thought tonight. Why don't you and I connect again tomorrow?
objections.rep_response: Asked 'What else would you say that you need to think about before making, feeling confident enough to make a decision?' and later argued that the best data point is lived experience rather than a written comparison.

objections.raw_quote: very honestly, Farooq, at 4k, if I can get somebody who will hold my feet to the fire in person, that's a no-brainer. I know kettlebell, this is very important, and Trevor can do that for me. But, at that price point, I might as well have somebody who I can go to who can see me and start to work with me.
objections.rep_response: Asked how he would decide between the options, then offered an unlisted one-month 'love it or leave it' trial at $1,200 as a way to get lived experience before choosing.

objections.raw_quote: committing to something is not the issue. Funding is fine, right? You can fund it. It's more like, hey, can I keep up? Can I do this? And can I feel good about doing this? ... I need some proof points is the best way I could describe it.
objections.rep_response: Explained the upgrade credit — start with three months and pay only the difference to extend — then offered the $1,200 trial.

offer.payment_plan_terms: Mentioned only in passing — 'Most people typically pop it on a credit card, but we have in-house payment plan options if necessary.' No structure discussed; the prospect stated funding was not an issue.
offer.guarantee_mentioned: For the trial: 'It's a month. 1,200 bucks. If after, you say this isn't for you, we shake hands, leave as friends... If it's the opposite, we can just process the difference, whether it's the three, the six, or the 12.' Also an upgrade-credit policy on the main tiers: 'if you come to three and you want to do six months, we charge you 2K as opposed to another 4K.'

evidence: No decision, no payment, no link. Explicitly deferred: 'I will give it some thought tonight' and 'let's regroup tomorrow and let's decide whether we move forward or not'
A concrete next call was agreed and diarised — Monday the 11th at 4pm Eastern, after Friday and Saturday were ruled out by his son's visit and Sunday by Mother's Day

He committed to a competing evaluation in the interim: 'I'm going to actually go check out my other option. Just because that's more local, and just see what the difference is, and what the cost looks like'
Positive signals: called the $1,200 trial 'that's actually quite a good way to do it' and 'that's fair', and said he might even do twelve months
Counter-evidence on intent: rated trust in the programme only 'five or six', and stated the decision would be made on a written comparison of criteria against the local in-person option
Affordability was explicitly not the blocker: 'Financially, I don't need to think'
outcome.next_step: Rebooked call for Monday 11 May at 4pm Eastern. Prospect to price a personal trainer at his golf club and compare on written criteria, and to consider the $1,200 one-month trial as a middle path. He offered to bring the call forward if his due diligence work freed up.

notable.note: The most ICP-aligned prospect in this batch by a distance — successful executive, health genuinely the neglected domain, funding explicitly not an issue — and he is the one who did not buy. His blocker was value against a comparable in-person alternative he can price locally, and the rep's answer was an analogy the prospect immediately dismantled: told he could learn from LeBron James online rather than a good coach in person, he replied 'it depends on where you're starting, right? If you can't get the ball in, LeBron's not going to be able to help you virtually.' Two further points. The rep explicitly declined to run the consequence frame, saying 'there's no point in me going into the doom and gloom.' And the single strongest emotional lever on the call — his mother's death in November and wanting to be around for three children, which he offered in his first minute — was acknowledged once and never returned to across fifty-six minutes.

quality.notes: Sustained inversion; whole passages of the rep's pillar delivery sit under the prospect's label and vice versa. Roles resolved from content. Two specific artefacts: at 00:04:49 the rep's question 'And how old are you?' is answered with a height, so age 58 is taken from the prospect's own opening statement and height from the follow-up; and the opening exchange 'I take it, you're single' / 'Oh, I am' is inverted — read in context with 'That's the other reason to be down there, I imagine', it is the prospect asking the rep about living in Medellín, and the prospect is in fact married. Most importantly, this file contains two entirely separate sales calls with two unrelated prospects; only the first is named in the title. The second begins at 00:56:14.
